seo.title: How to Build a Dashboard with Next.js | Admin Panel Guide
seo.description: Build an analytics dashboard with Next.js featuring charts, data tables, real-time updates, and role-based access control.

introduction: Dashboards are one of the most common web applications — from analytics platforms to admin panels to internal tools. Next.js is ideal for dashboards because server components handle data-heavy pages without shipping large JavaScript bundles, and the App Router's nested layouts keep your sidebar and navigation persistent across pages. This guide builds a complete analytics dashboard with charts, data tables, server-side filtering, and role-based access control.

prerequisites.name: Node.js 20+
prerequisites.description: Required for Next.js and its build tools.

prerequisites.name: PostgreSQL Database
prerequisites.description: For storing dashboard data, user accounts, and analytics. Neon offers a generous free tier.

prerequisites.name: React and TypeScript Knowledge
prerequisites.description: Familiarity with React hooks, component composition, and TypeScript interfaces.

steps.title: Scaffold the Project and Install Dashboard Dependencies
steps.description: Create a Next.js project and install libraries for charts, data tables, and database access. Recharts provides composable React chart components, and TanStack Table gives you headless data table primitives that you style with Tailwind. Prisma handles all database queries with type safety.

code_snippet.code:
npx create-next-app@latest my-dashboard \
  --typescript \
  --tailwind \
  --eslint \
  --app \
  --src-dir

cd my-dashboard
npm install recharts @tanstack/react-table @prisma/client next-auth@beta
npm install -D prisma

tips: Recharts is the most popular React charting library — it uses SVG rendering for crisp visuals at any resolution.
TanStack Table is headless, meaning you control all the markup and styling.

steps.title: Create the Dashboard Layout with Sidebar Navigation
steps.description: Build a persistent layout with a collapsible sidebar, top navigation bar, and content area. Next.js App Router layouts persist across page navigations — the sidebar does not re-render when you switch between dashboard pages. This gives the dashboard a native app feel.
tips: Use a server component for the layout to fetch the user session without client-side JavaScript.
Store sidebar collapse state in localStorage via a client component wrapper.

steps.title: Build the Overview Page with KPI Cards
steps.description: Create the main dashboard page with key performance indicator cards that show metrics like total revenue, active users, conversion rate, and growth percentage. Each card fetches its data from the database using a server component — no loading states needed because the data is available before the HTML reaches the browser.
tips: Use Promise.all to run independent database queries in parallel — this cuts the page load time significantly.
Calculate percentage changes by comparing current period to previous period.

steps.title: Add Interactive Charts with Recharts
steps.description: Build a chart component that visualizes time-series data like revenue over time, user signups, or page views. Recharts requires client-side rendering for interactivity (tooltips, hover effects), so mark it as a client component. The data is still fetched on the server and passed as props.
tips: Use ResponsiveContainer to make charts resize automatically with the viewport.
Keep chart components as client components but fetch and aggregate data in the parent server component.

steps.title: Build a Data Table with Server-Side Pagination
steps.description: Create a sortable, paginated data table using TanStack Table and URL search params for server-side pagination. Storing pagination state in the URL means table pages are shareable and work with the browser's back button. The server component fetches only the current page of data from the database.
tips: Server-side pagination keeps your queries fast even with millions of rows — you only fetch one page at a time.
Use Prisma's count and findMany in a Promise.all for parallel execution.

steps.title: Implement Role-Based Access Control
steps.description: Add role-based access control so admins can manage users and settings while viewers can only see analytics. Create a middleware layer that checks the user's role on every request and a utility function for component-level permission checks. Roles are stored in the database and cached in the session.
tips: Use a role hierarchy so admin inherits all editor permissions, and editor inherits viewer permissions.
Check permissions in server components and API routes — never rely on client-side role checks alone.

steps.title: Add Real-Time Updates with Server-Sent Events
steps.description: Implement real-time dashboard updates using Server-Sent Events (SSE) through a Next.js route handler. SSE is simpler than WebSockets for one-way data streams like live metrics. The client receives updates automatically and re-renders the affected components without polling.
tips: SSE automatically reconnects if the connection drops — the browser handles this natively.
Use a 10-30 second interval for dashboard updates to keep database load manageable.

steps.title: Deploy with Caching and Performance Optimization
steps.description: Deploy the dashboard to Vercel with optimized caching strategies. Dashboard pages with real-time data use dynamic rendering, while settings and documentation pages use static generation. Use React Suspense boundaries for streaming so the page shell loads instantly while data-heavy sections load progressively.
tips: Use Suspense boundaries to stream heavy components — the page shell renders immediately while charts load.
Create skeleton components that match the dimensions of their real counterparts to prevent layout shift.
Use 'force-dynamic' on pages that show real-time data, and let Next.js statically generate pages that rarely change.

next_steps: Add data export functionality (CSV, PDF) for reports and analytics.
Implement audit logging to track who changed what and when.
Build a notification system with in-app alerts and email digests.
Add keyboard shortcuts for power users to navigate the dashboard faster.
